songs.name: Beat It On Down The Line

ai_show_review.summary: Epic Dark Star > The Other One with tight electric set
ai_show_review.blurb: The February 13 1970 Fillmore show delivers a monster second set highlighted by an expansive Dark Star into The Other One and a scorching Lovelight. Jerry’s guitar is in top form, Phil locks in solidly, and the band rides a relentless groove throughout. Good Lovin', Black Peter, Hard To Handle and Saint Stephen stand out as tight, high‑energy moments.
ai_show_review.review:
On February 13, 1970 at the Fillmore East, the Dead rolled out one of their most electrifying early‑year performances. After a concise first set that included crisp renditions of Good Lovin', Black Peter and Hard To Handle, they launched into a second set that has become legendary among collectors – an hour‑and‑a‑half of pure improvisational fire. Dark Star swells into The Other One with Jerry Garcia’s tone described as “perfect” and “driving,” while Phil Lesh’s bass riffs weave tightly with Pigpen’s organ and the twin drummers’ thunderous pulse. The band stays locked in, delivering a soaring Lovelight that caps the set, and they close the night with a rousing encore of Casey Jones. Across six pristine soundboard captures the playing is consistently praised as “tight,” “inspired,” and “monster‑groove,” making this show a must‑listen for any Deadhead.

The Miller SBD (gd1970-02-13.sbd.miller.97613.sbeok.flac16) stands out as the definitive source – crystal‑clear, balanced, and free of drop‑outs, it lets every nuance of the performance shine. Even the good audience recordings capture the magic, but the soundboard’s fidelity makes the Miller tape the go‑to for both newcomers and archivists.

best_recording.reason: Pristine, balanced soundboard capture with excellent clarity and no drop‑outs; consistently praised as the clearest version of this legendary show.

key_highlights: Epic Dark Star → The Other One sequence that defines the second set.
Tight, groove‑driven performances of Good Lovin', Black Peter, Hard To Handle and Saint Stephen.
Miller SBD provides crystal‑clear audio, making every instrument shine.

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar tone is described as perfect and driving; his lead work on Dark Star and The Other One is repeatedly highlighted as inventive and stellar.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh’s bass riffs lock in tightly with the rest of the band, providing a solid foundation and even pairing powerfully with Pigpen during The Other One.
band_performance.Bob: Weir delivers strong rhythm guitar and vocal work, driving the high‑energy moments of the set, especially on Saint Stephen.
band_performance.Mickey: Drum work earns admiration for a powerful solo within The Other One, adding extra intensity to the groove.
band_performance.Billy: Shares the driving rhythmic foundation with Mickey, contributing to the tight, relentless feel of the electric set.
